local_figures.caption_scope: **Figure 2. An H409-centered design hypothesis on EGFR domain III.** The blue surface marks the recorded 16-residue patch on the 6ARU-derived chain-A target; L325, Q384, H409, Q411 and K465 are labeled hotspot residues. Numbers refer to mature EGFR; add 24 for UniProt P00533 precursor numbering. H346 was investigated separately and is not labeled here. This target crop illustrates site selection, not an experimentally demonstrated pH switch. [Structural reference: 6ARU](https://www.rcsb.org/structure/6ARU).

local_figures.caption_scope: **Figure 3. A proposed inter-protomer epitope on TNF-α.** Blue marks the 17 residue copies selected across chains A and C of the canonical-sequence predicted trimer used for design: A85–92, A125, A127, A131, A135, C32–34 and C146–147. Gray shows the remaining target surface. Numbers refer to the mature 157-residue TNF chain. The image shows the target patch; no designed binder or histidine-mediated interaction is depicted.

local_figures.caption_scope: **Figure 4. Pocket guidance and intracellular avoidance on GLP1R.** Blue marks Q234, W306 and R310 in canonical human numbering; salmon marks the proposed 29-residue intracellular-side avoidance map. The target is a WT-reverted, sparsely resolved 6X18-derived receptor preparation: full sequence representation does not supply coordinates for missing regions. No membrane plane is shown. The colors describe design guidance, not a validated agonist pharmacophore or an enforced membrane barrier. [Structural reference: 6X18](https://www.rcsb.org/structure/6X18).

local_figures.caption_scope: **Figure 5. Pilot guidance on a single-chain TfR1 proxy.** Blue marks N206 and L209 on chain A of the 11QC-derived target, using canonical/author numbering. Salmon marks the proposed avoidance surface intended to discourage binding near the omitted dimer partner. Only the single receptor chain is depicted; the full A/B dimer remained the evaluation reference. The initial 112-residue and later 71-residue avoidance prescriptions were distinct from the successful diagnostic arm, which requested no avoidance selections. Neither this view nor the guidance establishes dimer compatibility, pH switching or brain transport. [Structural reference: 11QC](https://www.rcsb.org/structure/11QC).

local_figures.caption_scope: **Figure 6. Peptide-focused guidance for KRAS-G12D pMHC design.** The 7OW6-derived design crop contains HLA-A*11:01 residues 1–182 and the separate ten-residue peptide VVVGADGVGK. Blue highlights peptide A5, D6 and V8; generation used either D6 or the alternative A5/V8 pair. D6 corresponds to KRAS Asp12 and is Gly6 in the WT peptide, which is not shown. Salmon marks HLA background/cut-face avoidance residues. The HLA α3 domain and β2-microglobulin were omitted from generation and are not depicted. A contact with the mutant peptide alone would not establish mutant specificity. [Structural reference: 7OW6](https://www.rcsb.org/structure/7OW6).
